text:
Marta: Evening swap — I'm off at 20:30 UTC. Quick notes for the shift: intermittent prefetch KV alerts in eu-west encoders, occasional encoder tail-latency spikes (~99p) after short request bursts, and noisy alert churn from kv-prefetch-ttl. Not an incident but this is the watchlist for tonight. I'll list actions below.

Evan: Thanks — are these tied to the caching canary deploy tonight?

Marta: Probably related. Canary 3 (cache_prefetch_ttl tweak) goes at 23:45 UTC. If you see an uptick in kv misses, fallback will hit encoder pools and might push tail latency. Two quick items: 1) I muted kv-prefetch-ttl noisy-repeats for 30m in eu-west; 2) a PR to increase hysteresis on the prefetch rate rule is in flight (PR #3428).

Jamie: Where did you mute? I need the unmute procedure if we roll back.

Marta: Muted in the PagerDuty integration under "eu-west-prefetch" — command I used:
```
alertctl mute --alert kv-prefetch-ttl --scope eu-west --duration 30m --reason "swap coverage"
```
Unmute is the same command with `--unmute`.

Sofia: Noted. Any dashboards I should watch? Which nodes showed the spikes?

Marta: Dashboards: /dashboards/encoders/latency-tail and /dashboards/prefetch/kv-miss-rate. Nodes: encoder-pool-eu-standby {node-7, node-12} showed repeated 99p spikes during the 21:10 burst. Pasted a minimal log snippet for context:
```
[21:10:34] kv_fetch: miss for key=pfx_abc size=128 origin=canary shard=7
[21:10:35] encoder: tail_latency=312ms request_id=... node=node-7
```

Evan: Cool. If tail spikes correlate with CPU steal or host OOM, we should drain. Any signs of host-level problems?

Marta: No CPU steal or OOM. Looks like request fanout during cache warmup after invalidation — repeated prefix misses, not host resource exhaustion.

Jamie: I'll keep an eye on encoder latency and be ready to drain node-7 if p99 crosses 350ms for >5m. Who's oncall for EU at 23:45?

Sofia: I'm EU oncall 23:00-07:00. I'll be watching the canary and will ping @Evan if rollback needed.

Marta: Other FYIs:
- Canary config: cache_prefetch_ttl=45s -> 300s in canary. If kv-miss-rate > 5% sustained for 5m, autopause should kick.
- There's a related noisy metric alert 'prefetch-rate-surge' firing because of the synthetic traffic flood test earlier; that's ticket #1981. Don't chase it unless you also see real p99 increases.
- If you see rapid alert churn, escalate in #eng-sre and I'll re-open the hysteresis PR immediately.

Evan: Suggest we add a temporary suppression rule for metrics tagged with the synthetic test so alerts stop oscillating.

Marta: Agreed. Added suppression: `alert-suppression add --tag synthetic-test --duration 4h`.

Jamie: Heads up — small rollout for the encoder scheduler tweak at 02:00 UTC tomorrow (unrelated) but could affect tail latency if combined with cache warmup. I've noted it in the ops calendar.

Sofia: Copy. My plan: monitor the two dashboards, mute chatter if it's clearly synthetic, and escalate if p99 > 300ms for 10m or kv-miss > 6% for 5m.

Marta: One last note — logs retention for prefetched keys rotated yesterday; if you need older traces, ask me before I leave. Leaving the handoff doc here: /hand-offs/2418302469. Thanks team.

oncall-bot: Reminder: shift swap recorded. PagerDuty is set to Sofia for EU 23:00-07:00.

Sofia: Thanks bot, and thanks team :thumbsup:
